title: Pre-Analysis — Flap Track Fairing Attachment Against the Wing Wiring Route
abstract: Closed work order checking the flap track fairing attachment change against the wiring that disconnects at each fairing, cancelled when the wiring office confirmed the disconnect could move with the attachment.

sections.objective: Establish whether the twin-lug flap track fairing attachment conflicts with the wing wiring that disconnects at each fairing, and whether the disconnect position has to move with the attachment. The work order was raised late, after the design was substantially complete, which is reflected in how quickly it closed.
sections.findings_summary: There is no conflict. The wiring disconnect sits eighty millimetres inboard of the attachment on the twin-lug arrangement and the wing wiring sheet already carries both positions with effectivity, which the wiring office had put there when the design was first circulated and which nobody in the structures office had noticed. The work order therefore found that the coordination it existed to perform had already happened through the wiring sheet. The removal task carries both the single-lug and the twin-lug release sequences and needed nothing. The one substantive observation is that the drain fitting, which is the point of the change as much as the attachment is, has no inspection requirement of its own beyond a walk-around look, and a drain that has been painted over will look the same as one that has not.
sections.next_steps: Cancel the work order; the coordination had already taken place. Raise the drain inspection observation separately with the maintenance programme owner. No changes to the modification or to any document.
